facts.text: Italian actor Luigi Montefiori, famous as George Eastman, directed this under the name "G. L. Eastman." It's the only film he ever directed alone.
Early on, the Chancellor says head office sent Sally Donnelly (Catherine Baranov) down from New York to audit Dr. Houseman. Later scenes show her living locally with her son, a continuity slip.
In Spain this was sold as "Re-Animator 2," pretending to be a sequel to Stuart Gordon's 1985 Re-Animator. It isn't.
Joe Bob Briggs showed this movie on Joe Bob's Drive-In Theater, in an episode that first aired January 25, 1992.
Although it's an Italian production, it was shot around Norfolk, Virginia with mostly unknown American actors, so it would pass as a US movie.
Reviewing the 2015 Blu-ray, Patrick Bromley gave the film 2 out of 5 and called it "a humorless slog" where the gore and rubber monster arrive too late to help.
Actress Catherine Baranov (Sally Donnelly) was a waitress at the hotel where the cast and crew were staying.
DVD Talk's review spotted borrowings beyond The Fly: Re-Animator's young-vs-old faculty rivalry, Jekyll and Hyde blackouts, and The Shining's stalking of a mother and son.
Laura Gemser, the Emanuelle star who plays the ill-fated prostitute here, also designed the costumes, as she did on Troll 2.
Richard Scheib of Moria called it "essentially a copy of US-made films of the era," and gave it one star.
Star Gene LeBrock (Dr. Peter Houseman) had just finished Fortress of Amerikkka before this. He later became a filmmaker and composer, according to Mondo Digital.
Director George Eastman's best-known acting role: cannibal killer Klaus Wortmann in Joe D'Amato's 1980 gore classic Antropophagus (aka The Grim Reaper), which he also wrote.
Severin's 4K Blu-ray, announced after director George Eastman died in May 2026, rescanned the original camera negative and adds interviews with Eastman, D'Amato and effects artist Maurizio Trani.
Eastman took his Americanized stage name when he was cast as a heavy in late-1960s and 1970s Spaghetti Westerns.
Eastman was a 6'9" former graphic designer before becoming an Italian genre-film heavy, working in westerns, horror, giallo, post-apocalyptic action and porn.
Clive Davis's book Spinegrinder: The Movies Most Critics Won't Write About dismisses the film as a "boring FLY remake rip-off."
Scott Aaron Stine's Gorehound's Guide to Splatter Films of the 1980s called it "entirely derivative of Cronenberg's The Fly" and said Eastman "should've stuck to acting."
Another 1990 horror film about scientists mutated by their own research is also titled Metamorphosis. Reviewer Esme Grey of Triskaidekafiles noted the mix-up when covering this one.
Genre Grinder noted the university setting is borrowed from Re-Animator, and that the third act turns to slasher tropes lifted from Joe D'Amato's own Absurd.
IMDb's connections list this Italian creature feature as referencing three famous films: The Shining, E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial and Cronenberg's The Fly.
The production company was Filmirage, Joe D'Amato's label, which also gave directors like Michele Soavi and Umberto Lenzi work in the late '80s and early '90s.
The film's tagline, as listed on TMDB, was "Witness the Change!"
Cinematographer Gianlorenzo Battaglia gave the film a soft, smeary look similar to his work on Witchery and Delirium.
DVD Talk's reviewer said the largely American cast "had rarely stood in front of a camera before or since," while calling leading man Gene LeBrock a movie-star look without the acting to match.
Special effects were by Maurizio Trani, and the keyboard score was composed by Luigi Ceccarelli.
Star Gene LeBrock also headlined Claudio Fragasso's Beyond Darkness (1990), released in Italy as "La Casa 5" to pose as an Evil Dead sequel.
In Germany the film was released as "Lizard – Die totale Mutation." The Lexikon des internationalen Films said it lacked the tension of The Fly.
In Britain the film was released as "Regenerator." Italian audiences knew it as "DNA formula letale."
The hospital dolly shots were achieved by pushing the camera on a wheelchair.
The needle-in-the-eye shot used a real pig's eye.
Imperial Entertainment's US VHS used gimmicky embossed packaging with LED lights and sound effects, which is why the tape stuck in memory.
The film was shot with live English sound, a rarity for Italian genre films of the era, which were usually dubbed afterward.
Mondo Digital notes the plot resembles The Lawnmower Man, which came out two years after this film.
Cut versions exist. A Japanese VHS reportedly runs the full 96 minutes, while the widely available cut is about 91-92 minutes.
Scream Factory's 2015 US Blu-ray paired this with Beyond Darkness. It was censored for an R rating in North America, though that disc appears to be unrated.
The film has circulated in cheap public-domain-style multi-packs like Mill Creek's Chilling Classics, often with poor transfers.
Eastman quit acting after directing this film to focus on screenwriting. He didn't return to acting until Pupi Avati's Christmas Rematch in 2003.
A 2023 German mediabook titled Lizard - Die Totale Mutation has an LED push button on the cover and claims 96 minutes, but Mondo Digital found the disc holds the 91-minute cut.
